title: High molecular gas content and star formation rates in local galaxies that host quasars, outflows, and jets
question: Do powerful z~0.1 type 2 quasars with kpc-scale ionized outflows and jets show signatures of AGN feedback (depletion or excitation) in their total molecular gas reservoirs, measured from unresolved APEX CO(2-1) and CO(6-5)?

recipe.goal: Flag, combine IFs and baseline-subtract APEX scans
recipe.method: Flag spike channels by eye per day, flag leading 150 (80 for CO(6-5)) and trailing 10 channels, combine the two spectrometers per sideband and polarisation, subtract a linear baseline in CLASS
key_parameters: baseline excludes ~500 km/s either side of the line (or the expected line position from the SDSS redshift when no line is seen)

recipe.goal: Reject poor scans, convert K to Jy, co-add and resample
recipe.method: Remove scans whose rms in 50 km/s bins exceeds a cutoff times the theoretical rms, scale each day to Jy with the APEX efficiency tool, combine spectra and resample to 1 km/s with a final linear baseline
key_parameters: rms / rms_t cutoff 1.25-2, chosen by visual examination and by minimising the final rms in 100 km/s bins

recipe.goal: Fit the line with a Gaussian by MCMC and derive upper limits
recipe.method: Single Gaussian line with free flux, peak velocity, width and Gaussian noise; emcee posterior medians as values, 16th/84th percentiles as errors, 3 sigma upper limits from the 99.7th percentile
key_parameters: 100 walkers, 500 steps, first 300 steps discarded as burn-in
assumptions: Gaussian noise; single Gaussian line profile

recipe.goal: Check for contamination in the APEX beam using ALMA CO images
recipe.method: Compare higher-resolution ALMA CO(3-2) (and CO(1-0) for J1356+1026) images with the APEX beam to find bright companions; only J1010+0612 has one, ~82 per cent of flux in the primary
assumptions: No CO flux falls outside the APEX beams, so no beam correction is applied

recipe.method: Solomon et al. 1997 formula L'CO = 3.25e7/nu_rest^2 * D_L^2/(1+z) * f
assumptions: Luminosity distances from the adopted flat LCDM cosmology (H0=70, OmegaM=0.3, OmegaLambda=0.7)

recipe.goal: Adopt SED-derived stellar mass and SFR and compute distance from the main sequence
recipe.method: CIGALE UV-IR SED fits (from Jarvis et al. 2019); SFR from L_IR,SF with the Kennicutt & Evans relation scaled by 0.94 for Kroupa to Chabrier; Delta_MS as sSFR relative to the Sargent et al. 2014 main sequence, starburst if Delta_MS ~4 or more

recipe.goal: Derive molecular gas masses, gas fractions and depletion times
recipe.method: Mgas = alpha_CO x L'CO(1-0), with L'CO(1-0) from L'CO(2-1) using r21=0.8; alpha_CO from the Tacconi-consistent recipe (Bolatto13/Genzel12 geometric mean with Genzel15 mass-metallicity relation) and, for xCOLD GASS comparison, from the Accurso17 relation with Kewley08 metallicity
assumptions: r21 = 0.8 (observed range 0.4 to 1.2 across AGN samples)

recipe.goal: Compare L'CO, gas fractions and depletion times with literature samples
recipe.method: Compare L'CO versus L_IR with Sargent14; fit log-linear relations to the Tacconi18 sample with AGN removed and measure median log vertical offsets of our sources; compare gas fraction against [OIII]/Hbeta with xCOLD GASS
key_parameters: Tacconi18 comparison limited to within +/-0.05 of the sample redshift range, CO-based measurements only

recipe.goal: Constrain CO excitation from the CO(6-5)/CO(2-1) ratio
recipe.method: Form r62 = L'CO(6-5)/L'CO(2-1) limits for three targets and compare with SLED predictions of Narayanan14 and with observed r62 distributions
